title: WPCRL/1104/2013 of Sapan Chopra AND ANOTHER Vs Senior Superintendent Of Police AND OTHERS

paras.text:
CLMA No. 13468 of 2013
In
WPCRL No. 1104 of 2013
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
Mr. Harshpal Sekhon, Advocate,
present for the petitioners.
Mr. M.A. Khan, A.G.A., present for the
State.
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Advocate, with
Mrs. Monika Pant, Advocate, present for the
respondent no. 3.
Rejoinder affidavit filed in the Court
today. Same is taken on record.
Heard.
By means of this writ petition, the
petitioners have sought quashing of the FIR
dated 15.09.2013, registered as FIR No. 74 of
2013, relating to offences punishable under
section 498A, 323, 504 and 506 IPC and one
punishable under 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition
Act, at Police Station Sadar (R.O.P. Basant
Vihar) District Dehradun.
This petition was heard on 19.09.2013,
and the matter was referred to the Mediator
for exploring every possibility of mutual
settlement between the parties and the Court
directed that till further order petitioners shall
not be arrested pursuant to the FIR in
question. The matter was placed before the
Mediator on 28.10.2013. Both the parties
appeared before him. The matter was again
taken up on 27.11.2013 on which date also
both the parties appeared before the
Mediator. Joint as well as individual sessions
of mediation were held between both the

parties but parties did not arrive at any
settlement, and mediation proceedings were
closed.
I have heard Mr. Harshpal Sekhon,
counsel for the petitioners, Mr. M.A. Khan,
A.G.A. for the State and Mr. Arvind
Vashistha and Mrs. Monika Pant counsel for
the respondent no. 3. I have considered their
submissions and also gone through the FIR.
From the perusal of the FIR, the offence is
clearly made out. It is for the Investigating
Officer to investigate the matter and to reach
at conclusion and thereafter file charge sheet
or final report in the matter.
Considering the submission of learned
counsel for the parties, I am not inclined to
interfere in the matter. It is not a case where
FIR should be quashed by the Court.
Therefore, the writ petition is dismissed.
However, it is observed that in case the
petitioners surrender/appear before the court,
their bail application shall be considered
expeditiously.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Parul 16.12.2013
